teaching_target: Divergence at a constructive margin: arrows apart, magma rising into the central opening and solidifying, new crust at the centre carried outward.
viewing_direction: vertical cross-section across a mid-ocean ridge
question_shows: arrows pointing away from the centre in plates R and S
central opening (labelled) with a magma-filled fissure from a magma body
crust age bands with a newest-to-oldest key
independent_solution: arrows point away from the centre -> plates move apart (1)
magma reaches the opening and cools there (1)
newest crust at the centre, older outward on both sides -> new crust carried outward (1)
assumptions: Not to scale; age bands are schematic, not dated.
Symmetry is idealised; the notes state perfect symmetry is not required in reality.
